title: I couldn't find a way to play ARC anymore, so I made a browser game inspired by it
author: Silent_Ad1589
selftext:
I used to love ARC (Attack, Retrieve, Capture) growing up, the old top-down ship combat game. Years later I wanted to play something like it again, and it was hard to find anything. So I started building my own. 

Being honest: I found Armor Critical late, when this was mostly built. It looks a lot closer to the original, and it's in beta, so if you want the real ARC feel, go check it out. SaucerJam is inspired by ARC, not a copy. It's meant to be a small, free thing for the community that I keep improving based on what players say. 

What I cared about most is that it opens instantly on any device: phone, tablet or desktop, in a browser tab, with no install and no account. You can play a round on a break, or send a friend a link and they're in your room seconds later, whatever device they're on. 

Three weapons share one energy bar: a laser, a ricochet that banks off walls, and a grenade that arcs over cover. The map opens more districts as more people join. Built with Claude Code (Opus), three.js and a Node server; music by Suno. 

Try it (empty rooms fill with bots after 10 seconds, so you'll get a real match solo): [https://menezmethod.itch.io/saucerjam](https://menezmethod.itch.io/saucerjam) If you played ARC back then, I'd really like to hear what it gets right and what it's missing.
